- **A control event raised from Load runs inside it,** before the statement that raised it returns.
- **Clearing the name doesn't end a loaded form.** The instance lives on, and Terminate waits for the unload and the
  end of the procedure that was running in it.

### Bare names in a form, for implicit `Me` (2026-10-14, #995)

The same harness, native and p-code agreeing on every row; one project per row, so a compile error stays its own.
Form1 holds `Text1`; Module1 holds the logger.

| Form code | VB6 |
|---|---|
| `hWnd = 5` (bare, and as `Me.hWnd = 5`) | does not compile: "Function or interface marked as restricted, or the function uses an Automation type not supported in Visual Basic" |
| `Count = 1`, `Me.Count = 1`, `HasDC = True`, `hDC = 5` | the same message, for each |
| `Set ActiveControl = Text1` | compiles; the run stops at a modal dialog before logging, which the harness's timeout cut off |
| `Option Explicit`, then `Caption = "set"` and `Caption & "\|" & Me.Caption` | `set\|set` |
| `Cls`, then `TextWidth("abc") > 0` and its `TypeName` | `cls ok`, then `True Single` |
| `Dim Caption As String` in Load, `Caption = "local"`, then `Caption & "\|" & Me.Caption` | `local\|Form1` |
| `TypeName(ScaleWidth)`, `ScaleWidth > 0`, `TypeName(Controls)`, `Controls.Count` | `Single True`, `Object 1` |
| `Hide` in Load, then `Visible` | `hidden False` |
| `Name`, `Left("abc", 2)`, `Left = Me.Left` | `Form1 ab True` |
| `Caption(1)`, where Module1 has `Public Function Caption(ByVal n As Integer) As String` | does not compile: "Wrong number of arguments or invalid property assignment" |
| `Tag(2)`, where Module1 has `Public Function Tag(ByVal n As Integer) As String` | the same |
| `Left(5)` | the same |
| `Left("abc", 1, 2)` | the same |
| `Left$("abc", 2)` and `VBA.Left("abc", 1)` | `ab a` |
| `Left(5)` in Module1, not the form | does not compile: "Argument not optional" |

What these show:
- **Assigning a member the Form only reads is refused at compile time,** with a message about restricted functions,
  not one about read-only properties. That held for every read-only member tried, bare and through `Me`.
- **A bare member is the form's under `Option Explicit` too,** and a local of the same name shadows it.
- **A bare method runs,** as `Cls` does, and one called for its value returns its value, as `TextWidth` does.
- **A property called with arguments** is VBA's function when the call fits it, and otherwise refused as the
  property's, never a project Function of the name.

The Form's members themselves were read out of VB98\VB6.OLB by `scripts/dump-typelib-members.ps1`, into
`vb6-form-members.json`: 87 names on `_Form`, its default interface, and 31 events on `FormEvents`. `Print`, a method
of a form in VB6 code, is not in the type library: VB6 compiles it as syntax.

### HexIDE

Read from the code at `upstream/main` c933fbd, not run. A form's code runs as the primary standard module of an
interpreter of its own, and `Me` and the form's name are bound to the window (`VBLoader.RunForm`). So:
- **Implicit `Me`:** a bare name is never looked up on the form: `Caption = "x"` makes a new variable (#995).
- **A form's Public Subs:** the form is a standard module, so they are found unqualified from another module, where VB6
  refuses (#822). And a name the form shares with another module's Public Sub is "Ambiguous name detected: Ping"
  (`TryResolveProcedure` counts the form as a second standard module with a `Ping`), where VB6 runs the module's.
- **The form from outside:** its name is bound in its own module only.
- **`TypeName(Me)`:** it is the window's .NET class name with `VB` taken off, `FormRuntime`.
- **The lifecycle:** Initialize and Activate are never raised, and Resize comes before Load (#994). A form's declarations
  never run (#256). `Unload` stops the run (#973).

#822 carries the design that makes the form an instance. #995 follows it for implicit `Me`, and the predeclared,
auto-instantiating name belongs to the slices that bring `Load`, `Show` and a second form.

#822's first slice makes the startup form an instance of its module, with `Me` that instance. It brings the rows
above into line for `Me`, `TypeName(Me)`, the form reached from a module, both of the Public Sub rows, the
declarations at Initialize, and Initialize and Load before Resize. A control used in Initialize (#1009), Activate, the
predeclared name and `Unload` remain.

#994 then brings in Activate and Deactivate, and Resize once on the first show rather than for each size the
window reports: [A form's Resize, Activate and Deactivate](#a-forms-resize-activate-and-deactivate-2026-10-23-994).

#995 then brings implicit `Me` into line: a bare name in a form's code is the form's member, after its locals, variables,
controls and procedures and before the project's globals, for reads, assignments and calls. A member VB6's Form has and
HexIDE does not is refused as not implemented, rather than made a variable. A read-only one assigned is VB6's compile
error. A property called with arguments is VBA's only for `Left` with its two, and otherwise refused, never a project
procedure: refused as not implemented, because the error VB6 gives depends on whether the property's type takes an index.

## Assigning to a control property (2026-10-12, #768)

Measured to decide what `Label1.Caption = 5` stores, and what every other property does with a value of another
type. Real `vb6.exe` 6.00.8176 (SP6), guest locale **en-GB** (decimal point `.`, thousands separator `,`).

**Harness.** One Standard EXE, `Startup="Form1"`, with `Label1`, `Text1`, `Command1`, `Check1` and a disabled
`Timer1` (Interval 500). Four `/make` runs over PowerShell Direct, each `Form_Load` writing a log and ending
with `End`. The exe ran in the guest's session 0. Nothing here needs painting, so the interactive-session rig was
not needed. Every probe is one line under `On Error Resume Next`:

```vb
Label1.Caption = "(unset)": Err.Clear: Label1.Caption = 5: e = Err.Number: W "Label.Caption = 5", e, Label1.Caption
```

So each row resets the property first, and a refused assignment shows as the reset value, unchanged. `W` logs
the value read back, its `TypeName`, and the `Err.Number` the assignment raised.

### A String property takes CStr of anything

| Assignment | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `Label1.Caption = 5` / `= -7` / `= Variant 42` | `5` / `-7` / `42` | 0 |
| `= 1.5` | `1.5` (the locale's decimal separator) | 0 |
| `= CSng(1) / 3` | `0.3333333` | 0 |
| `= 1E+20` / `= 12345678901234#` / `= CCur(2.5)` | `1E+20` / `12345678901234` / `2.5` | 0 |
| `= 0.1 + 0.2` / `= CSng(1E+7)` | `0.3` / `1E+07` | 0 |
| `= True` / `= False` | `True` / `False` | 0 |
| `= Empty` | (empty string) | 0 |
| `= #1/2/2003#` / `= #10:30:00 AM#` / `= #1/2/2003 10:30:00 AM#` | `02/01/2003` / `10:30:00` / `02/01/2003 10:30:00` | 0 |
| `= Null` | `(unset)`, **unchanged** | **94** |
| `Text1.Text`, `Command1.Caption`, `Check1.Caption`, `Me.Caption` `= 5` | `5` | 0 |
| `Text1.Text = Null`, `Me.Caption = Null` | unchanged | **94** |
| `Label1.Tag = 5` / `= True` / `= CSng(1) / 3` | `5` / `True` / `0.3333333`, **`TypeName` String** | 0 |
| `Label1.Tag = Null` | unchanged | **94** |

**This is coercion-on-store, exactly** (see that section): a String property behaves as `Dim s As String : s = x`,
Null included. And **`Tag` is a String**, not a Variant: `TypeName(Label1.Tag)` is `String` after `Tag = 5`.

### A numeric property converts, and refuses what it cannot convert before changing

| Assignment | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `Label1.Left = "300"` | `300` (`Single`) | 0 |
| `Label1.Left = "abc"` / `= ""` | unchanged | **13** |
| `Label1.Left = Null` | unchanged | **94** |
| `Label1.Left = Empty` / `= True` | `0` / `-1` | 0 |
| `Label1.Left = 1.5` / `= "1.5"` / `= 2.5` / `= 2.4` | **`2`** / **`2`** / **`2`** / `2` | 0 |
| `Label1.Left = "1,5"` | **`15`** | 0 |
| `Label1.Left = 1E+20` | unchanged | **6** |
| `Timer1.Interval = "1000"` / `= 2.5` / `= 3.5` | `1000` / `2` / `4` (`Long`) | 0 |
| `Timer1.Interval = "abc"` / `= Null` / `= 3000000000#` | unchanged | 13 / 94 / **6** |
| `Timer1.Interval = 65535` | `65535` | 0 |
| `Timer1.Interval = 65536` / `= True` | unchanged | **380** |

### An enum or colour property converts, then range-checks with 380

| Assignment | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `Check1.Value = 1` / `= "1"` / `= 2` | `1` / `1` / `2` (`Integer`) | 0 |
| `Check1.Value = 1.5` / `= 1.6` / `= 2.5` | `2` / `2` / `2` | 0 |
| `Check1.Value = 2.6` / `= 3` / `= -1` / `= True` | unchanged | **380** |
| `Check1.Value = "abc"` / `= ""` / `= Null` / `= 40000` | unchanged | 13 / 13 / 94 / **6** |
| `Label1.MousePointer = n`, n from 0 to 15, and 99 | `n` | 0 |
| `Label1.MousePointer = -1`, `16`, `17`, `98`, `True` | unchanged | **380** |
| `Label1.MousePointer = "2"` / `= 40000` | `2` / unchanged | 0 / 6 |
| `Check1.Appearance = 0` / `= 1` | `0` / `1` | 0 |
| `Check1.Appearance = -1`, `2`, `3`, `True` | unchanged | **380** |
| `Label1.BackColor = "255"` / `= 255.6` / `= "&HFF"` | `255` / `256` / `255` (`Long`) | 0 |
| `Label1.BackColor = True` / `= -2` | unchanged | **380** |
| `Label1.BackColor = 1E+20` / `= Null` | unchanged | 6 / 94 |

The OLE_COLOR range, probed byte by byte:

| High byte | Low 24 bits accepted | Refused (380) |
|---|---|---|
| `&H00` (RGB) | any | |
| `&H01` (palette index) | `&H000000` to `&H00FFFF` | `&H010000` and above (`&H1010000`, `&H1FFFFFF`) |
| `&H02` (palette-relative RGB) | any (`&H2000000`, `&H2000001`, `&H2FFFFFF`) | |
| `&H80` (system colour) | `&H00` to `&H18` | each of `&H80000019` to `&H80000020` (probed one by one for #774), `&H80000030`, `&H80000100` |
| `&H03`, `&H04`, `&H7F`, `&HC0`, `&HFF` | | all (`&H3000000`, `&H4000000`, `&H7FFFFFFF`, `&HC0000000`, `&HFF000000`) |

That is OLE's own colour validation, as far as it was probed. `&H18` is `COLOR_INFOBK`, the last entry of the
table VB6 exposes; the refusal from `&H19` on is measured, not inferred from Windows' `COLOR_*` numbering, which
has a hole at `&H19` and goes on past it.

**A palette colour is kept as given** (measured for #774): `&H1000001` reads back `16777217`, `&H100000F`
`16777231`, `&H100FFFF` `16842751`, `&H2000001` `33554433` and `&H2FFFFFF` `50331647`, each the same Long that was
assigned. What it paints as was not measured.

### The rule

**A property assignment is coercion-on-store into the property's type, plus a range check that a declared variable
does not have.** The conversion raises 13, 94 or 6 exactly as `Dim x As T : x = value` would. A value that converts
but is not one the property accepts is **380, Invalid property value**, and that is how `True` fails for an enum:
it converts to -1. The order matters and is measured: `Check1.Value = 40000` is **6**, not 380, so the Integer
conversion comes before the range check. Nothing is changed when either step refuses.

### What this overturned, or found

- **`Left` is not a Single inside, though it reads back as one.** `Left = 1.5` reads back 2, and so does 2.5
  (half to even). `Left = 1E+20`, which a Single holds easily, is Overflow. A position is held as a whole number
  of twips in a Long. That twips are the unit is inferred from the default ScaleMode, since the probe did not
  change it.
- **`"1,5"` is fifteen**, not one and a half, and not an error: in the en-GB locale the comma is a thousands
  separator, and VB6 skips it. HexIDE's string-to-number rule allows none and raises 13 (#770). Not probed: a
  locale whose decimal separator is the comma.
- **`MousePointer` 4, 5, 13 and 14 are accepted.** `VBCursorType`'s comment called them gaps in VB6's numbering.
  They are not (#120). Their names and pointers are measured under "MousePointer's names and pointers".
- **`Tag` is a String.** HexIDE declared it as an object and stored whatever it was given.
- **`CStr` of a Date leaves out what is zero.** A midnight date has no time, and a time has no date. HexIDE wrote
  both (#771). A Single shows seven significant digits and a Double fifteen. HexIDE showed more (#772). Both were
  fixed by #779; see "Turning a number or a date into text".

### Measured for the review of #774

The same harness, three more `/make` runs, with an `HScrollBar` added (Min 0, Max 100, and a second set in the
`.frm` to Min 100, Max 0).

**A scroll bar's `Value` is range-checked, from a String too, and either way round:**

| Assignment (Min 0, Max 100, reset to 10) | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `HScroll1.Value = "50"` / `= 100` / `= "100"` | `50` / `100` / `100` | 0 |
| `= 101` / `= 150` / `= "150"` / `= -1` / `= "-1"` | `10`, **unchanged** | **380** |

| Assignment (Min 100, Max 0, reset to 100) | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| (as loaded) `Min`, `Max` | `100`, `0` | 0 |
| `Value = 50` / `= 0` / `= 100` / `= "50"` | `50` / `0` / `100` / `50` | 0 |
| `= 150` / `= -1` / `= True` | unchanged | **380** |
| `= "abc"` | unchanged | 13 |
| `= Empty` | `0` | 0 |
| `= 2.5` / `= 99.5` | `2` / `100` (half to even) | 0 |

So a bar whose Min exceeds its Max is legal, and the range check takes the two either way.

**A Boolean property is CBool**, and CBool of Empty is False:

| Expression or assignment | Value | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `CBool(Empty)` | `False` | 0 |
| `CLng(Empty)` / `CDbl(Empty)` | `0` (Long) / `0` (Double) | 0 |
| `CBool("")` | | 13 |
| `Command1.Enabled = Empty` / `= 0` (reset to True) | `False` / `False` | 0 |
| `Command1.Enabled = Null` / `= ""` | `True`, **unchanged** | **94** / **13** |

**.NET's NaN and Infinity are not VB6 numbers:**

| Expression or assignment | Value | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `CDbl("NaN")`, `CDbl("Infinity")`, `CDbl("-Infinity")`, `CLng("NaN")` | | **13** |
| `CDbl("1E+400")` | | **6** |
| `Label1.Left = "NaN"` / `"Infinity"` / `"-Infinity"` / `"1.#INF"` / `"1.#QNAN"` | unchanged | **13** |
| `Val("NaN")` | `0` (Double) | 0 |

**A hex String wraps at the target's width, and a trailing `&` in it is refused:**

| Expression | Value | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `CLng("&H8000000F")` / `CDbl("&H8000000F")` / `Val("&H8000000F")` | `-2147483633` (Long / Double / Double) | 0 |
| `CLng("&HFFFFFFFF")` / `CLng("&O37777777777")` | `-1` | 0 |
| `CLng("&H100000000")` | | 6 |
| `CDbl("&H100000000")` | `4294967296` | 0 |
| `CLng("&HFFFF")` / `CLng("&H8000")` / `CLng("&H10000")` | `65535` / `32768` / `65536` | 0 |
| `CInt("&HFFFF")` | `-1` (Integer) | 0 |
| `CDbl("&H10&")`, `CLng("&HFFFF&")`, `CLng("&H8000000F&")` | | **13** |
| `Text1.BackColor = "&H8000000F"` / `= "-2147483633"` | `-2147483633` (Long), a system colour | 0 |
| `Text1.BackColor = "&H8000000F&"` | unchanged | 13 |

**A colour reads back as its Long, and a hex literal is typed by its digits:**

| Statement, after `Text1.BackColor = &HFF` | Value | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `Text1.BackColor` | `255` (Long) | 0 |
| `Text1.BackColor = 255` / `Text1.BackColor = vbRed` | `True` / `True` | 0 |
| `Text1.BackColor + 1` | `256` (Long) | 0 |
| `Text1.BackColor = &HFF00` | unchanged | **380** |

**A control where a value is wanted is its default property:**

| Statement | Result | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `s = Text1` / `s = Label1` (s As String) | `"Text1"` / `"Label1"`, the Text and the Caption | 0 |
| `v = Text1` / `v = Command1` / `v = Check1` (v As Variant) | `"Text1"` String / `False` Boolean / `0` Integer | 0 |
| `Label1 = "x"` / `Text1 = "y"` / `Check1 = 1` | Caption `x` / Text `y` / Value `1` | 0 |

**`ListIndex` is an Integer with a range of -1 to ListCount - 1**, the same in a ListBox and a ComboBox (one more
`/make` run, three items added in `Form_Load`, and an empty ListBox beside them):

| Assignment (three items, reset to 0) | Reads back | Err |
|---|---|---|
| `List1.ListIndex = 2` / `= -1` / `= "1"` | `2` / `-1` / `1` | 0 |
| `= True` / `= Empty` | `-1` / `0` | 0 |
| `= 1.5` / `= 2.5` | `2` / `2` (half to even) | 0 |
| `= 3` / `= "3"` / `= -2` | `0`, **unchanged** | **380** |
| `= 40000` | unchanged | **6**: an Integer overflows before the range is checked |
| `= Null` / `= "abc"` | unchanged | 94 / 13 |
| `Combo1.ListIndex = 2` / `= "1"` / `= -1` | `2` / `1` / `-1` | 0 |
| `Combo1.ListIndex = 3` / `= -2` | unchanged | 380 |
| `List2.ListIndex = -1`, empty list | `-1` | 0 |
| `List2.ListIndex = 0` / `= -2`, empty list | `-1`, unchanged | 380 |

**`CBool` reads a number in a String as `CDbl` does** (one more expression batch): `CBool("NaN")`,
`CBool("Infinity")`, `CBool("-Infinity")` and `CBool("1.#INF")` are 13, `CBool("1E+400")` is 6, and `CBool("&H10")`
is `True`. `CStr(Empty)` is `""`.

### What the review's measurements overturned

- **`&HFF00` is not a green.** A test written for #774 restored `&HFF00` through a Variant and expected it back.
  VB6 refuses it with 380, because four hex digits make an Integer literal, and `&HFF00` is -256, which is no
  colour. The Long `&HFF00&` is the green. That was our own expectation, and it was wrong.
- **A trailing `&` belongs to the literal, not to a String.** HexIDE trimmed it from `"&H10&"`; VB6 raises 13.
- **The width a hex String wraps at follows the target.** `CLng("&HFFFF")` is 65535, and `CInt("&HFFFF")` is -1.
  Whether `CInt` wraps at 16 bits for more than four digits was not measured.
- **`CDbl("1E+400")` was Infinity in HexIDE**, where VB6 raises 6. .NET parses it to Infinity without complaint,
  exactly as it parses the word `"Infinity"`.
- **`Enabled = Empty` is False with no error.** HexIDE raised 13, because its CBool sent Empty through the
  String-to-number parse. The code comment beside it already said False.

### HexIDE, after #774

Property assignment goes through `VbNumeric.CoerceOnStore` and the measured range checks above, in
`AvaloniaInteroperability.ConvertForAssignment` (and `CheckScrollBarValue` for a scroll bar's `Value`).
`HexIDE.Integration.Tests` `PropertyAssignmentTests` covers, through real controls and the interpreter:
- the String-property rows, the Single, Double, Currency and Decimal ones included, since #779;
- the position, `Interval`, scroll bar `Value`, `Enabled`, `CheckBox.Value`, `MousePointer` (error only, #769) and
  `BackColor` rows, the colour checked as stored and as left unchanged;
- copying a colour from one control to another, through a Variant, and into a caption;
- Null into `Tag`, and the two `Tag` idioms below.

`ConversionFunctionsTests` covers CBool of Empty, the NaN and Infinity spellings, and `CDbl("1E+400")`.

`ListIndex` is range-checked as measured, and it and a scroll bar's `Value` convert as an Integer, so
`ListIndex = 40000` is 6. That the scroll bar's `Value` is 6 there too is inferred from its `TypeName`, Integer, and
was not measured. `Tag = Empty` stores `""`; it used to end the run as Internal error 51. `CBool` reads its number
through `CDbl`'s parse.

A Date into a String property is written as `CStr` writes it, in the program's locale: `Label1.Caption = #1/2/2003#`
reads back `02/01/2003` under en-GB, as measured above. It was refused until the interpreter had the user's locale
(#777, #794), because before that it would have put the month first on every machine.

**Refused with `NotImplementedException`, rather than answered wrong:**
- **A palette colour** (#786), from any type. HexIDE has no colour that holds one.
- **`Value` on a scroll bar whose Min exceeds its Max** (#787). Avalonia raises Maximum to Minimum, so the value
  would read back clamped.
- **A control, an array or an object on the right** of a property assignment. For a control, VB6 reads its default
  property (#790). (Superseded for a class instance and the in-box objects by #840, "An object used as a value": a
  class with no default member raises 438, one with a default member is refused naming #174, and Err stands for its
  Number. A control and an array are still refused here.)
- **A colour read from a Timer or a scroll bar** (#801). VB6 gives neither control a colour, but both bind one as
  every templated control does, so the read would give black. Until #795 a Label's and a TextBox's colours were
  refused here too, because neither loaded them where a read could find them; both read back now, as measured
  under "A Label's colours, read back and painted".

**Where HexIDE still differs:**
- **`Tag` holds what it is given**, not a String: `Tag = 5` reads back the Integer 5, where VB6 has `"5"`. Making
  it a String waits on #211, because `If Tag = 1` and `Tag + 1` rely on it. An unset `Tag` reads back `""`, and
  Null is 94, as in VB6.
- ~~**Positions are not rounded to whole twips** (#791).~~ They are since #933, which holds them in twips at the
  property: see *A control's position at run time*.
- **A comma in a numeric String** (#770).
- **A hex String** (#788): `BackColor = "&H8000000F"` is an Overflow, and `"&H8000000F&"` is accepted.
- **Reading a control as a value** outside a property assignment (`s = Text1`) gives a .NET type name (#790).
- **Not measured:** `Label1.Caption = o` with `o` set to `Nothing` never reaches the conversion in HexIDE; what
  VB6 raises there is unmeasured.


## A list's members: ListCount, List(i), AddItem's index and RemoveItem (2026-10-22, #821)

What do a ListBox's and a ComboBox's list members do, in range and out of it? Three `/make` probes, each built native
and p-code, all six builds agreeing line for line. Each runs in Form_Load after `Me.Show`, under `On Error Resume Next`,
on four controls: a ListBox, a ComboBox with Style 0 (Dropdown Combo), one with Style 2 (Dropdown List), and a ListBox
with `Sorted = True`. **The four agree on every row** but the two marked, so the table gives one answer.

Each control starts with `c`, `a` and `b` added, in that order, which the sorted list keeps as `a`, `b`, `c`. A row's
`ListIndex` and `ListCount` are read after it.

| Statement | VB6 |
|---|---|
| `ListCount`, empty, then with three items | `0`, `3`, an **Integer** |
| `ListCount = 5` | compile error **"Can't assign to read-only property"** |
| `List(0)`, empty | `""`, Err 0 |
| `List(0)`, `List(2)` | `c`, `b`, Strings (sorted: `a`, `c`) |
| `List(3)` (= ListCount), `List(-1)`, `List(-2)`, `List(100)` | `""` each, **Err 0** |
| `List("1")`, `List(1.6)` | `a`, `b`: the index is converted to an Integer, rounding |
| `List(40000)` | Err **6** Overflow |
| `List("q")` | Err 13 |
| `List(Null)` | Err 94 |
| `List()` | compile error "Argument not optional" |
| `ListIndex = 1`, then `List(1) = "B"`, the selected item | replaced; **no Click**, `ListIndex` 1; a ComboBox's `Text` becomes `B` |
| `List(3) = "d"` (= ListCount) | **appended**, ListCount 4, Err 0 |
| `List(-1) = "z"` | **appended**, at the end, Err 0 |
| `List(10) = "e"`, past ListCount | Err **381** "Invalid property array index" |
| `List(-2) = "y"` | Err **-2147024882** "Out of memory"; nothing added. A **ComboBox's `ListIndex` moves from 1 to 2** |
| `AddItem "z", 0`, with the item at 1 selected | inserted at 0; **`ListIndex` 2**, the selection follows its item; no Click |
| `AddItem "y", ListCount` | appended |
| `AddItem "w", ListCount + 1`, `AddItem "v", -1`, `AddItem "w", 10` | Err **5** "Invalid procedure call or argument" |
| `AddItem "u", "1"` | inserted at 1: the index is converted |
| `AddItem "x", 40000` | Err 6 |
| `AddItem "n", Null` | Err **13**, not 94 |
| `AddItem Null` | Err 94 |
| `AddItem "z", 0` on the **sorted** list | inserted at 0 all the same: `z` first, before `a` |
| `AddItem "q", 0`, empty; `AddItem "r", 2`, one item | the first inserted; the second Err 5 |
| `RemoveItem ListCount`, `RemoveItem -1`, `RemoveItem 10`, `RemoveItem 0` empty | Err 5 |
| `RemoveItem 40000` | Err 6 |
| `RemoveItem 0`, with the item at 3 selected | removed; `ListIndex` 2; no Click |
| `ListIndex = 0`, then `RemoveItem 0`, the selected item | removed; `ListIndex` **-1**; no Click from the removal; a ComboBox's `Text` becomes `""` |
| `ListIndex = 1`, then `RemoveItem 0` | removed; `ListIndex` 0 |

What these show:
- **A ListBox and a ComboBox of either style are one list.** Only `Text` and the one row below tell them apart.
- **Reading is forgiving and writing is not.** Any `List(i)` read that converts to an Integer is `""` outside the
  list, while a write outside it is an error. The exceptions are `ListCount` and `-1`, which both append.
- **AddItem takes 0 to ListCount and RemoveItem 0 to ListCount - 1**, and both raise 5 outside that. An index converts
  as an Integer argument does: a String that reads as a number is taken, past 32767 is Overflow.
- **The selection follows its item** through AddItem and RemoveItem, and empties when its item is removed. None of them
  raises Click.
- **`Sorted` does not override AddItem's index.**

What resisted explanation:
- **`List(-2) = "y"` raises "Out of memory"**, -2147024882 (`0x8007000E`, E_OUTOFMEMORY), where 381 would be the
  obvious error, and on a ComboBox only, it moves `ListIndex` from 1 to 2 though nothing was added. Presumably the
  write reaches the window as an insert at position -2, which the control refuses as if memory had run out; no rule
  here explains the ComboBox's selection moving.
- **`List(-1) = "z"` appends** rather than raising, as if -1 meant "at the end".
- **`AddItem "n", Null` is 13 where `List(Null)` and `AddItem Null` are 94.**

### HexIDE

Before #821, `ListCount` and `List(i)` were "Method or data member not found", `RemoveItem` was not implemented, and
`AddItem` appended whatever its index said.

Since #821, `ListMembers` gives a ListBox and a ComboBox every row above but two.
- **`List(i)`** is caught by name with its index, on the read path in `ExpressionExecutor` and the write path in
  `StatementExecutor`, before the property lookup that would find the design-time `List` instead.
- **An index converts** by `VbNumeric.CoerceOnStore` to an Integer, which gives 6, 13 and 94 as measured. AddItem's
  Null index is 13 before it.
- **The selection** follows its item through AddItem and RemoveItem because Avalonia's does. A replaced item loses its
  selection in Avalonia, so `List(i) =` sets it back.
- **381's text** was HexIDE's "Invalid property-array index", unmeasured; it is now VB6's "Invalid property array
  index".
- **Pinned** in `ListMembersTests`, on a ListBox and a ComboBox.

What it still does not do:
- **A ComboBox's `ListIndex` moving 1 to 2 after `List(-2) = "y"`.** HexIDE leaves it where it was. The error is
  raised, and no program is likely to read the selection after it.
- **A Dropdown List's `Text`** (#1428). A Dropdown Combo's two `Text` rows run as measured since #926.
- **`Sorted`,** which HexIDE has no property for.
- **`ListCount = 5`** is the compile error's text, raised when the statement runs, not before the program does.

## A ComboBox's Text, at each Style, from code (2026-10-22, #926)

**The probe.** A form with four ComboBoxes, built with `/make` and run, native and p-code giving byte-identical logs:
- `Combo1`, Style 0 (Dropdown Combo), saved with `Text = "Combo1"`;
- `Combo2`, Style 1 (Simple Combo), saved with `Text = "Combo2"`;
- `Combo3`, Style 2 (Dropdown List), with no Text line;
- `Combo4`, Style 2, saved with `Text = "x"`.

Each of the first three was filled with `apple`, `Banana` and `cherry`, then given each Text in turn. Every handler for
Click and Change logged its name, and each row was read under `On Error Resume Next`.

| Read at load | VB6 |
|---|---|
| `TypeName(Combo1.Text)` | **String** |
| `Combo1.Text`, `Combo2.Text` | `Combo1`, `Combo2`, as saved |
| `Combo3.Text`, and **`Combo4.Text`, saved as `x`** | `""` each: **a Dropdown List ignores a saved Text** |
| `ListIndex` of each | -1 |
| `Style` of each | `0`, `1`, `2`, an **Integer** |

| Statement | Style 0 and Style 1, alike | Style 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `Text = "Banana"`, an item's text | Text `Banana`, **`ListIndex` -1**, **Change** | selects it: `ListIndex` 1, **Click** |
| `Text = "banana"`, its text in other case | Text `banana`, `ListIndex` -1, Change | `Banana`, already selected, stays so; Text `Banana`; **Click all the same** |
| `Text = "Ban"`, `"zz"` or `""` | that Text, `ListIndex` -1, Change | Err **383**, nothing changed, no event |
| `Text = "cherry"` | Text `cherry`, Change | selects it, `ListIndex` 2, Click |
| `ListIndex = 0` | Text `apple`, `ListIndex` 0, **Click, and no Change** | Text `apple`, Click |
| `ListIndex = -1` | Text `""`, Click, no Change | Text `""`, Click |
| `Text = Null` | Err **13**, not 94; nothing changed | Err 13 |
| `Text = 5` | Text `5`, Change | Err 383 |

What these show:
- **A Style 0 or 1 combo's Text is its edit box's,** free of the list. Setting it to an item's text selects nothing, and
  every assignment here raised Change. The second probe, below, asks what this one did not.
- **A Style 2 combo's Text is its selected item.** Setting it selects the first item whose whole text matches without
  regard to case, and raises Click every time. With no match it is 383, "'Text' property is read-only".
- **Moving `ListIndex` changes a Style 0 combo's Text** without raising Change.

**A second probe,** the same way, on a Style 0 and a Style 1 combo filled with `apple`, `Banana` and `cherry`. The two
styles gave the same rows, and native and p-code the same logs:

| Statement | VB6 |
|---|---|
| `Text = Text`, unchanged | nothing: **no Change**, `ListIndex` -1 still |
| `ListIndex = 1` | Text `Banana`, Click |
| `Text = "zz"`, with item 1 selected | Text `zz`, **`ListIndex` -1**, Change |
| `Text = "cherry"`, another item's text, with item 1 selected | Text `cherry`, **`ListIndex` -1**: it selects nothing; Change |
| `Text = "Banana"`, the selected item's own text | **nothing**: `ListIndex` 1 still, no Change |
| `Text = "banana"`, that text in other case | Text `banana`, **`ListIndex` -1**, Change |
| `ListIndex = 2`, then `ListIndex = 2` again | Click the first time, **none the second** |
| `Text = "cherry"`, with item 2, `cherry`, selected | nothing |
| `Clear` | Text `""`, `ListIndex` -1 |

So **a Style 0 or 1 combo's `Text = s` does nothing when `s` is its Text already,** compared exactly. Otherwise it puts `s`
in the edit box, clears the selection and raises Change.

What resisted explanation:
- **`Text = Null` is 13, Type mismatch,** where a TextBox's `SelText = Null` and the list's `List(Null)` are 94.

### Drawn in the VB6 IDE's designer

**The probe.** In the guest's console session, the VB6 IDE opened a project holding an empty Form1. Each toolbox icon was
double-clicked, which adds that control to the form at its default size, centred: a TextBox, then three ComboBoxes. Style
was set in the Properties window by Ctrl+Shift+S, the value's number and Enter, and the form saved with Ctrl+S. Every
step was checked by a screenshot. The saved blocks:

| Drawn | What the designer wrote |
|---|---|
| TextBox | `Text = "Text1"`, Height 495, Width 1215 |
| ComboBox, Style left at 0 | `Text = "Combo1"`, Height 315, Width 1215 |
| ComboBox, Style set to 1 | `Style = 1 'Simple Combo`, `Text = "Combo2"`, Height 315 |
| ComboBox, Style set to 2 | `Style = 2 'Dropdown List`, **no Text line**. The designer still showed `Combo3` in the box |
| That combo, Style set back to 0 | `Text = "Combo3"` |
| Combo1 given `Text = zz` in the Properties window | `Text = "zz"` |
| Then Style 2 | the Properties window's **Text read `Combo1`** |
| Then Style 0 again | `Text = "Combo1"`: the `zz` is gone |

What these show:
- **A drawn TextBox or ComboBox starts with its own name as its Text,** as its Caption would be for a control that has
  one. The names count from 1 (#540).
- **Setting Style to 2 resets the Text to the control's name,** and a Dropdown List's Text is never written. Going back
  to 0 or 1 writes that name.

Not measured: what Style 2 does in the designer to a combo whose Name has been changed, which would show whether it is
the name now or the name the control was drawn with.

### In HexIDE (#926)

- **A drawn TextBox or ComboBox** starts with its name as its Text, and a control with no Caption is no longer given one.
- **A Dropdown Combo's and a Simple Combo's Text** reads and writes at run time as both probes measured. That includes
  `Null` as 13, and the two #821 rows in which the selected item's text follows it. Avalonia's editable combo would select
  the item a Text matches, without regard to case, so while code sets the Text every item reads as a text no program can
  set, and none matches.
- **A Dropdown List's Text** is never written to the .frm, and is ignored at load. At run time, reading or writing it is
  refused as not implemented, naming #1428, because what it does there needs the Style modelled.
- **Click and Change** come as measured since #1429, which records them with real input.
- **Not done:** the designer resetting a combo's Text to its name when its Style becomes 2 (#1428).

## A ComboBox's Click, Change and DropDown, with real input (2026-10-22, #1429)

**The probe.** A form with a Dropdown Combo (Combo1), a Simple Combo (Combo2) and a Dropdown List (Combo3), each holding
`apple`, `Banana` and `cherry`. It drives itself from a Timer, run in the guest's console session where it has the
foreground:
- the mouse with `SetCursorPos` and `mouse_event`;
- the arrow button and each list item found with `GetComboBoxInfo`, `GetWindowRect` and `CB_GETITEMHEIGHT`;
- the keys with VB6's own `SendKeys`.

Each handler logged its event with `ListIndex` and `Text`. Native and p-code gave byte-identical logs, in both runs.

| Combo1, a Dropdown Combo | VB6 raised |
|---|---|
| click the arrow | **DropDown**, before the list shows |
| click `cherry` in the list | **Click**, `ListIndex` 2, Text `cherry`; **no Change** |
| type `x` | **Change**, Text `x`: the item's text was selected, so the key replaced it; `ListIndex` -1 |
| Backspace | Change, Text `""` |
| Up, list closed, nothing selected | **Click**, `ListIndex` 0, `apple`; no Change |
| Down, list closed | Click, `ListIndex` 1 |
| Home, Shift+End, type `apple` | **a Change per key**, `a` to `apple`, and **`ListIndex` -1 throughout**: typing an item's text selects nothing |
| F4 | DropDown |
| Down, list open | **Click at once**, `ListIndex` 2 |
| Down again, on the last item | nothing |
| Enter | **nothing**: the Click came with the move |
| F4, Up, list open, Escape | DropDown, Click at the Up; **Escape undoes nothing**, `ListIndex` stays 1 |
| Alt+Down, then Escape | DropDown, and nothing else |
| click the arrow, then the item already selected | DropDown, then **Click all the same** |

| Combo2, a Simple Combo | VB6 raised |
|---|---|
| click `Banana` in its list | Click, `ListIndex` 1 |
| type `x` | Change, Text `x`, `ListIndex` -1 |
| Down | Click, `ListIndex` 0 |
| click `Banana`, then click it again | Click, and **Click again** |

| Combo3, a Dropdown List | VB6 raised |
|---|---|
| click the arrow | DropDown |
| click `Banana` | Click, `ListIndex` 1 |
| Down, list closed | Click, `cherry` |
| type `a` | **Click**, `apple`: the first item starting with the letter |
| F4, Down, Down, Enter | DropDown, then a Click at each Down, `apple` then `Banana`; nothing at Enter |
| F4, Up, Escape | DropDown, Click at the Up, `apple`; Escape undoes nothing |
| click the arrow, then the item already selected | DropDown, Click |

What these show:
- **Click is a choice, not a change.** It comes from every pick of an item by the mouse, even of the item already
  selected, and from every arrow key that moves the selection, open or closed.
- **Change is the edit box's,** from typing and from code's Text. Choosing an item puts its text in the box with no
  Change.
- **Typing selects nothing** in a Dropdown or Simple Combo, even an item's whole text. A Dropdown List takes a letter as
  a pick.
- **DropDown comes as the list opens,** by the mouse, F4 or Alt+Down.
- Code: `ListIndex = n` raises Click when it moves the selection, and not when it doesn't. `Text = s` raises Change
  unless `s` is the Text already. Neither `Clear`, `AddItem`, `RemoveItem` nor `List(i) =` raises either (the oracle's
  "A ComboBox's Text" and "A list's members").

What resisted explanation:
- **F4 then Down, with Text `apple` and nothing selected, selected `Banana`,** not `apple`. So the open list seems to
  start from the item the edit box's text matches, though `ListIndex` read -1 in DropDown. One case is not a rule:
  whether the match is exact, without regard to case or by prefix is not measured.

### In HexIDE (#1429)

- **Every row above runs as measured** but that one, which is left out of the tests: there HexIDE's Down selects the
  first item.
- **Click is raised where the input is taken,** not from Avalonia's selection, which also moves for a list edit that
  raises nothing.
- **The arrow keys are the combo's own,** list open or closed. Avalonia's move only the focus in an open list, and from
  no selection its Up selects nothing.
- **Avalonia's editable combo selects the item a new Text matches,** without regard to case. Typing therefore reads every
  item as a text no one can type, and an item chosen whose text another shares, `Banana` and `banana`, stays chosen.
- **Not measured:** a Simple Combo's list, always shown in VB6, which HexIDE draws as a dropdown (#1428), and whether
  arrow keys, like the mouse, leave the chosen item's text selected in the edit box.

## Out of stack space — Error 28 (2026-08-22, #80)

Verified with a `Sub Main` probe (`/make`, run, append each line to a log so nothing is lost to buffering).

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `Sub A(): Call A(): End Sub`, `On Error GoTo` in the caller | **`Err 28`**, `"Out of stack space"` |
| depth reached before it raises | **258,825 frames** |
| the program afterwards | `2 + 2` = `4`, `Err.Number` = 0 — VB6 **does not terminate** |
| `Err.Raise 28` | same number and description |

**258,825 is the number that settles the design.** The fix for an interpreter is a *real stack probe*, not a
depth counter, because any counter a person would choose is two orders of magnitude below VB6's real
capacity — and wrong in the direction that breaks working programs rather than the one that catches broken
ones. HexIDE uses `RuntimeHelpers.TryEnsureSufficientExecutionStack()` at `RunProcedure`, the single sink
every user procedure, method, Property accessor and lifecycle hook flows through.

**Known divergence in depth, not in behaviour.** HexIDE's own frames are far fatter than compiled VB6's — an
async state machine plus an ANTLR visitor walk per call — so on a 1 MB Windows thread stack it reaches about
**202** frames for a bare `Call A(n + 1)` sub and **between 60 and 80** for a recursive Function. Linux
main threads get 8 MB and go several times deeper. That gap is tracked on its own; it is not a regression
from the guard, since the process was already dying at the same depth.

Two probes did **not** complete and their answers are still open:

- a recursive **Function** (`DeepFn = DeepFn()`) had not raised 28 after 120 s, where the equivalent Sub
  raises in well under a second. Whether VB6 gets much deeper in a Function or simply takes far longer is
  unmeasured;
- `On Error Resume Next` **inside** the recursive Sub ran for minutes without settling. Each frame swallows
  the error and carries on, so the unwind re-recurses; whether it terminates at all is unmeasured.

### Variant arithmetic promotes on overflow

First spotted while writing the #80 tests (an untyped `Fact(10)` should be 3628800 as a Long, and raised
Err 6 instead). Superseded by the fuller measurement in *Declared type, Variant subtype, and overflow
promotion* below, which has the whole ladder and the declared-vs-Variant rule that drives it.


## Infinity, NaN, and division by zero (2026-08-22)

VB6 has **no Infinity and no NaN**. IEEE-754 produces them; VB6 raises instead — so a result that is not a
VB6 number is always an error, never a value.

| Probe | Result | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `1E+308 * 10` | **Err 6** | infinite magnitude → Overflow |
| `1E+308 / 0.0001` | **Err 6** | same, through `/` |
| `1E+308 ^ 2` | **Err 6** | same, through `^` |
| `Exp(1000)` | **Err 6** | same, through an intrinsic |
| `CSng(3E+38) * CSng(10)` | **Err 6** | Single overflows at its own range |
| `(-2) ^ 0.5` | **Err 5** | NaN → Invalid procedure call |
| `0 ^ -1` | **Err 5** | infinite, but a DOMAIN error, so 5 and not 6 |
| `Sqr(-1)`, `Log(0)`, `Log(-1)` | **Err 5** | domain |
| `2 ^ 10` | `1024` Double | `^` is always Double |

`0 ^ -1` is the row worth keeping: the result is infinite, so the obvious rule says Overflow, and vb6.exe
says Invalid procedure call. No inspection of the result can get it right — the distinction is in the cause.

### Division by zero depends on whether the operands were DECLARED

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `a / b` with **Variant** operands (`a = 1`, `b = 0`) | **Err 6** |
| `a / b` with **declared** `Integer` or `Double` operands | **Err 11** |
| `1 / 0` (literals) | **Err 11** |
| `a \ b` by zero, declared or Variant | **Err 11** |
| `a Mod b` by zero | **Err 11** |

Real division by zero is *Overflow* on the Variant path and *Division by zero* everywhere else — the OLE
Automation `VarDiv` quirk, which maps a zero divisor to `DISP_E_OVERFLOW`. `\` and `Mod` are Err 11 either
way. HexIDE cannot express the Variant row yet: it has no notion of which operands were declared (see
*Declared variables do not retain their declared type* below), so it raises 11 for all of them.

## Declared type, Variant subtype, and overflow promotion (2026-08-22)

Three behaviours turn on the same distinction — **was this operand statically typed, or a Variant?** — and
HexIDE currently cannot tell, because a declared variable does not keep its type.

### A declared variable reports its declared type

| `Dim x As T`, `x = 3`, `TypeName(x)` | VB6 | HexIDE |
|---|---|---|
| `Integer` | `Integer` | `Integer` ✓ |
| `Long` | `Long` | **`Integer`** |
| `Double` | `Double` | **`Integer`** |
| `Single` | `Single` | **`Integer`** |
| `Byte` | `Byte` | **`Integer`** |
| `Currency` | `Currency` | **`Integer`** |
| `Boolean` / `String` | `Boolean` / `String` | ✓ |

The assignment overwrites the slot with the *literal's* subtype and the declared type is lost. `Dim` itself
is right — it seeds a correctly-typed zero — so this is purely an assignment-side loss.

### …and the declared type drives the result type

| expression | VB6 |
|---|---|
| `declInt * declLong` (30000 * 3) | `90000` **Long** — the ladder already widens; no promotion needed |
| `declInt * declDbl` (3 * 2) | `6` **Double** |
| `declByte * declInt` (100 * 3) | `300` **Integer** |
| `declByte * declByte` (200 + 200) | **Err 6** — Byte+Byte stays Byte |

`declInt * declLong` is the one that shows the cost: HexIDE raises Err 6 there, not because promotion is
missing but because it thinks the Long operand is an Integer.

### Variant arithmetic widens instead of overflowing

Byte → Integer → Long → Double, and **stops**. Currency, Decimal and Double are terminal — overflowing one
of those is Err 6 with no promotion.

| expression (Variant operands) | result | type |
|---|---|---|
| `CByte(200) + CByte(100)` | 300 | **Integer** |
| `30000 * 3` | 90000 | **Long** |
| `2147483647 + 1` | 2147483648 | **Double** |
| `2000000000 * 3` | 6000000000 | **Double** |
| `CSng(3E+38) * CSng(3)` | 9.0E+38 | **Double** |
| `CCur(9E+14) * 10` | — | **Err 6** |
| `CDec("7.9E+28") * 10` | — | **Err 6** |
| `1E+308 * 10` | — | **Err 6** |
| `variant * declInt` (30000 * 3) | 90000 | **Long** — one Variant operand is enough |
| `variant * literal` (30000 * 3) | 90000 | **Long** |
| `declInt * declInt` / literal-only | — | **Err 6** — no Variant, no widening |

Operators that widen: `+`, `-`, `*`, `\` (`CInt(-32768) \ CInt(-1)` = 32768 **Long**), unary `-`, and `Abs`.
`/` and `^` are always Double anyway. Assigning a widened result back into a declared variable range-checks
normally: `i = 30000 * 3` is Err 6, `l = 30000 * 3` is 90000.

> **This corrects the qualifier in *Arithmetic result types* above.** That table was measured entirely
> through declared variables, and its conclusion — "there is no overflow auto-promotion" — holds only there.


### Coercion-on-store — what a declared variable does to the value you put in it

| assignment | result | rule |
|---|---|---|
| `Dim s As String : s = 5` | `"5"` String | anything stringifies |
| `s = True` | `"True"` String | |
| `Dim b As Boolean : b = 5` | `True` | CBool: any non-zero |
| `b = "True"` | `True` | strings parse |
| `b = "banana"` | **Err 13** | and raise when they cannot |
| `Dim i As Integer : i = "12"` | `12` | a numeric target parses a String too |
| `i = "abc"` | **Err 13** | |
| `i = 12.6` / `i = 12.5` | `13` / **`12`** | half-to-even, not away-from-zero |
| `i = True` | `-1` | |
| `Dim b As Byte : b = 300` | **Err 6** | the declared range is enforced on store |
| `Dim x As T : x = Null` | **Err 94** | every T, String included |
| `x = Empty` | `0` / `""` | |
| `Dim l As Long : l = 3 : l = l + 1` | `4` **Long** | the declared type survives arithmetic |
| `Dim a(1 To 3) As Long : a(1) = 5` | `5` **Long** | array elements carry the element type |
| `a(2) = 30000 : a(2) * 3` | `90000` **Long** | …and widen like one |

### ByRef takes its type from the caller, because VB6 will not let it differ

`Call TakesLong(v)` with `v As Variant` and `Sub TakesLong(ByRef x As Long)` is a **compile error** —
*"ByRef argument type mismatch"*. So the two sides always agree, and a ByRef alias can inherit the caller's
declared type with nothing to convert at the boundary. (HexIDE does not reject it: compile-time argument
type checking needs a bound AST, which is the language engine's job, not HexIDE's.)


## The `Empty` literal (2026-08-22, #126)

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `TypeName(Empty)` | `"Empty"` |
| `VarType(Empty)` | `0` |
| `IsEmpty(Empty)` / `IsNull(Empty)` | `True` / `False` |
| an un-assigned `Dim u` | `TypeName(u)` = `"Empty"`, `u = Empty` is `True` |
| `Empty = 0` | **True** |
| `Empty = ""` | **True** |
| `Empty = False` | **True** |
| `Empty = Null` | **Null** — neither True nor False |
| `v = 5 : v = Empty` | clears the Variant; `IsEmpty(v)` is `True` |
| `Empty + 1` | `1` Integer |
| `Empty * 2` | `0` Integer |
| `Empty & "x"` | `"x"` |
| `Dim Empty As Integer` | **Syntax error** — it is a reserved word, not a name |

Empty coerces to its partner's **zero**, whatever kind of zero that is — `0`, `""` or `False` — which is
what makes all three comparisons True at once. Against `Null` the comparison stays Null, because Null
propagates and Empty does not stop it.

That last row is why `Empty` belongs in the lexer beside `NOTHING`/`NULL` rather than in the built-in
constants table: VB6 reserves the word, so a user variable must not be able to shadow it. (In ANTLR the
token has to be named `EMPTY_`, because `ParserRuleContext` already has a static `EMPTY` — the same
collision the vendored LSP grammar already works around for `NULL_`.)

## The `App` object — and the difference between F5 and a compiled exe (2026-09-01, #136)

One probe project, three deliberately different `.vbp` keys — `Name="NameKey"`, `Title="TitleKey"`,
`ExeName32="ExeNameKey.exe"`, saved as `DesignTime.vbp` — so every answer names its own source instead of
identical strings agreeing by coincidence. Run twice: compiled with `/make`, and under **F5 in the IDE**.

| | compiled `.exe` | design time (F5) |
|---|---|---|
| `App.Title` | `TitleKey"` — the `Title=` key | `TitleKey"` — same |
| `App.EXEName` | `ExeNameKey` — the exe's filename, no extension | **`DesignTime` — the `.vbp` filename** |
| `App.Path` | the exe's folder | the project's folder |
| `App.ProductName` | follows `Title` | **empty** |
| `App.PrevInstance` | `False` | `False` |
| `App.Major` / `Minor` / `Revision` | `1` / `0` / `0` | same |
| `CompanyName`, `FileDescription`, `LegalCopyright`, `Comments` | empty when the version keys are unset | same |

**`App.EXEName` at design time is the `.vbp` filename** — not `ExeName32`, and not the project `Name`.
Both of those were present and different, and neither is what came back. This is the row worth having
measured: guessing "the project name" is the obvious answer and it is wrong.

**`App.ProductName` is empty at design time** but follows `Title` once compiled — it is read from the
version resource, which only a built exe has.

**With no `Title=` key at all**, a compiled `App.Title` falls back to the project `Name=` (measured
separately: `Name="verify"`, no `Title=` → `App.Title` = `verify`).

### A VB6 defect: `Title=` keeps its closing quote

`Title="TitleValue"` yields `App.Title` = **`TitleValue"`**. `Title=UnquotedTitle` reads back clean, so it
is the quotes: VB6's `.vbp` reader strips the leading `"` and not the trailing one. It shows up under F5
as well as compiled, so it is the project-file reader rather than the resource writer.

This is not academic — **VB6's own templates write the key quoted**: `Title="Project1"` appears verbatim in
the `VB98\Template` corpus. So real VB6 projects carry a stray `"` at the end of `App.Title`.

**HexIDE strips both quotes.** Per the Fidelity Principle in `CLAUDE.md` — reproduce VB6's intended
behaviour, not its bugs — a trailing quote in an application's title is a defect, not a design. Recorded
here so the divergence is deliberate and traceable rather than a later "bug".

### Note on method

`scripts/vb6-oracle.ps1` covers the compiled column; the design-time column cannot be automated from here.
A `MsgBox` is modal, so a probe that opens one never writes its file unless something answers it, and reading a
caption from outside does not work either — a PowerShell Direct session cannot see the guest's interactive desktop and
enumerates zero windows session-wide. The F5 column was produced by pushing the project into the VM with
`Copy-Item -ToSession`, having a human press F5, and reading the output file back over the same session.
That is the pattern for any future design-time question.

**A compiled probe can answer its own `MsgBox` (2026-10-12).** A form `Timer` keeps firing while a `MsgBox` is
open in a compiled program. So the probe's own timer can find the box with `FindWindow`, read which buttons it
holds with `GetDlgItem`, and close or answer it with `PostMessage`. That needs no person and no view of the
desktop. It is how "RGB, QBColor and MsgBox's style" was measured, and its probe is the template. Only the F5
column still needs a person.
## `IsMissing`, and the shape of an omitted argument (2026-09-01)

`IsMissing` only means anything inside a procedure that has an `Optional` parameter, so this needed a probe
with its own procedures rather than the expression harness. No modal is involved, so it still ran headless
through `/make`.

| call | `IsMissing` | value |
|---|---|---|
| `Probe(1)` where `Optional v` | **True** | |
| `Probe(1, 2)` where `Optional v` | False | 2 |
| `Probe(1)` where `Optional v = 5` | **False** | 5 |
| `Probe(1)` where `Optional n As Integer` | **False** | 0 |
| `Probe(1, , 3)` where `Optional b, Optional c` | b **True**, c False | |
| `Probe(1)` where `a` is required | False | |

**An omitted argument is a Variant of subtype `vbError`** — `TypeName` = **`"Error"`**, `VarType` = **10**,
`IsEmpty` = False, `IsNull` = False, `IsError` = **True**. It is emphatically *not* `Empty`, and treating
it as Empty is what makes `IsMissing` impossible to express — the two are separate subtypes and VB6 tests
them separately.

**Two guesses the measurements overturned**, both of which would have shipped wrong:

- An `Optional` with a **declared type** is never missing. There is nowhere in an `Integer` to put a
  `vbError` Variant, so an omitted `Optional n As Integer` simply gets `0`.
- An `Optional` with a **default** is never missing either — the default supplies it, so `IsMissing` is
  False and the value is the default.

So `IsMissing` is True in exactly one situation: an `Optional` with neither a declared type nor a default,
left out by the caller (or left blank in the middle of the list — the last row ties this to #135, where a
blank argument keeps its position).

**Measured but not implemented:** using a missing value in a string concatenation raises **Error 13, Type
mismatch**. Recorded so the next person does not have to re-derive it; HexIDE currently lets such a value
flow rather than raising.

## A control VB6 cannot load renders as an empty box (2026-09-01, design-time)

**Verified**, by the human-in-the-loop method in *Note on method* above: a `.frm` citing an unregistered
OCX pushed into the VM, opened in `VB6.EXE`, screenshotted.

VB6 draws a control it cannot load as a **plain etched rectangle at the recorded position and size** —
nothing inside it. No diagonals corner-to-corner, no X, no type name, no control name, no icon. Just an
empty sunken frame where the control would be.

The recollection this was checked against was "an empty box with diagonal lines from each corner". That is
wrong **for VB6**, and it is the sort of detail worth having right before anyone draws one.

It may well be right about something else — VBA's editor, or a later Visual Studio — and that is the point
rather than a footnote. A crossed placeholder is a real thing someone has genuinely seen; it just is not
this product. This is the hazard `CLAUDE.md` names when it says VBA diverges from VB6 at the edges and
`vb6.exe` always wins: a memory can be perfectly accurate and still be about the wrong host. Which host it
came from was not worth chasing, because the only question that mattered — what VB6 draws — now has a
screenshot behind it.

The probe used a made-up GUID (`{A1B2C3D4-1111-2222-3333-444455556666}`, `NOSUCH.OCX`) with a real
`CommandButton` beneath it for scale; the box's width matched the button's `3015` twips, so the geometry
comes straight from the designer file's `Left`/`Top`/`Width`/`Height`.

### Why HexIDE should NOT copy it exactly

VB6's box carries meaning it does not itself supply: the developer reached it by dismissing a *"cannot load
control"* dialog seconds earlier, so an unlabelled rectangle is enough to say "the thing you were just told
about goes here".

HexIDE has no such dialog, and its box would mean something different — **not** "this OCX is missing from
this machine" but "HexIDE does not model this control", which stays true on a machine where the OCX is
correctly installed and registered. A developer following VB6 muscle memory would install the control,
reopen, see the same empty box, and reasonably conclude HexIDE is broken.

So: keep the geometry, which is VB6's intended behaviour and is exactly reproducible from the file; replace
the emptiness, which is a shortcoming rather than a design. Per the Fidelity Principle, a divergence — and
recorded here so it stays deliberate.

### Its size when the file records none, and what the box is (2026-10-22, #157)

**The question.** The probe above had a `Width` and `Height`. An ImageList records neither: `Web Browser.frm`'s has
`Left`, `Top`, `_ExtentX` and `_ExtentY` (HIMETRIC) and nothing else. The obvious guess is that the extents size it.

**The probe.** One form holding three controls of an unregistered class (a made-up GUID, `NOSUCH.OCX`), each beside a
real CommandButton of the size it should come out as. It was opened in VB6's IDE through the console agent. Each
control was then selected with Tab, and its position and size read from the toolbar's readout.

| Control | What the file records | VB6's readout |
|---|---|---|
| `Ext1` | `Left` 240, `Top` 240, `_ExtentX` 3528, `_ExtentY` 1764 (2000 × 1000 twips) | 240, 240, **1200 × 480** |
| `Sized1` | `Left` 240, `Top` 1680, `Width` 3015, `Height` 495, extents for 1000 × 500 | 240, 1680, **3015 × 495** |
| `Bare1` | `Left` 240, `Top` 3000, nothing else | 240, 3000, **1200 × 480** |

**What it shows:**
- **`Width` and `Height` size the box when the file has them, and 1200 × 480 twips when it has neither.** The extents
  play no part, so the guess was wrong: `Web Browser.frm`'s ImageList comes out 1200 × 480. A file recording only one
  of the two was not probed.
- **The box is a PictureBox.** The Properties window names each one "`Ext1` PictureBox". VB6's load log says first
  "Class NoSuchLib.Extent of control Ext1 was not a loaded control class", then "The property name _ExtentX in Ext1
  is invalid", and the same for `_ExtentY` and `_Version`. A PictureBox has none of the three. What VB6 writes when
  such a form is saved was not probed.
- **So its border is a PictureBox's, the sunken one.** The section above calls it both "etched" and "sunken"; it is the
  second. HexIDE's box (#157) is drawn sunken to match, and labelled, which is the divergence argued above.

## Bitwise And / Or / Xor / Not — the result-type ladder (2026-09-02, #166)

Measured with `scripts/vb6-oracle.ps1`. Every row below is `vb6.exe` output, not inference — and two of them
overturned what the implementation would otherwise have assumed.

### The result type is a ladder, not a widening

| left | right | result type |
|---|---|---|
| `Boolean` | `Boolean` | **Boolean** |
| `Boolean` | `Byte` | **Integer** |
| `Boolean` | `Integer` | Integer |
| `Boolean` | `Long` | Long |
| `Byte` | `Byte` | **Byte** |
| `Byte` | `Integer` | Integer |
| `Byte` | `Long` | Long |
| `Integer` | `Integer` | Integer |
| any | `Long` / `Single` / `Double` / `Currency` / numeric `String` | **Long** |

So the rule is: **both Boolean → Boolean; both Byte → Byte; otherwise the wider of the two, floored at
Integer.** Note the two exceptions that a plain "widen to the larger type" rule gets wrong — `Byte And Byte`
stays `Byte`, and `Byte And Boolean` jumps to `Integer` rather than staying `Byte`.

A numeric `String` yields **Long**, not Integer: `"12" And 10` is `8` as a `Long`.

### `Not` keeps its operand's width — including 8-bit for Byte

| expression | value | type |
|---|---|---|
| `Not CByte(5)` | **250** | **Byte** |
| `Not 5` | -6 | Integer |
| `Not CLng(5)` | -6 | Long |
| `Not True` | False | Boolean |
| `Not CDbl(5)` | -6 | Long |
| `Not "12"` | -13 | Long |

`Not CByte(5)` = 250 is the one to notice: `Byte` complements at **8 bits** (255 - 5), it does not widen to
Integer and give -6. The existing `TryUnpack<int>` comment — *"Byte widens to Integer (VB6: Byte arithmetic
promotes to Integer)"* — is correct for **arithmetic** and wrong for **bitwise**.

### Floating operands round to Long, banker's-style

| expression | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| `CDbl(2.5) And 3` | 2 | 2.5 → **2** (to even), `2 And 3` = 2 |
| `CDbl(3.5) And 3` | 0 | 3.5 → **4** (to even), `4 And 3` = 0 |
| `CDbl(2.4) And 3` | 2 | 2.4 → 2 |
| `CDbl(-2.5) And 3` | 2 | -2.5 → -2, `-2 And 3` = 2 |
| `CSng(2.5) And 3` | 2 | same for Single |

Round-half-to-even, which is .NET's `Math.Round` default — so the conversion is free rather than something
to hand-roll.

### Empty is an Integer zero; Null is NOT implemented and is not simple

| expression | value | type |
|---|---|---|
| `Empty And 5` | 0 | Integer |
| `Empty Or 5` | 5 | Integer |
| `Not Empty` | -1 | Integer |
| `Null And 5` | **Null** | Null |
| `Null And 0` | **0** | Integer |
| `Null Or 5` | **5** | Integer |
| `Null Or 0` | **Null** | Null |

`Empty` is implemented — it reduces to an Integer zero, which is all four of its rows.

**`Null` is measured here but deliberately NOT implemented**, because the rows do not fit the rule they
look like. A per-bit three-valued logic predicts `Null Or 5` is Null (the bits where 5 is zero stay
unknown); vb6.exe returns **5**. Whatever the real rule is, it is not the obvious one, and guessing it
would be exactly the mistake this document exists to prevent. `And`/`Or`/`Xor` continue to raise a type
mismatch on Null, unchanged, and the rule is left to the Null-propagation work that owns it.

### Boolean mixed with a number stays bitwise

`True And 2` is **2** (Integer), not `True`. `True` is -1, so `-1 And 2` = 2. `And` never becomes a logical
short-circuit operator: `True And True` is `True` only because `-1 And -1` is `-1`.
## DefType — default typing by first letter (2026-09-02, #169)

Measured with `scripts/vb6-oracle.ps1 -Declarations`, which this work added: `DefType` is a declarations-
section directive, so it cannot be probed as an expression, and it **cannot be measured with
`Option Explicit` on at all** — it is a rule about undeclared variables.

| probe (under `DefInt A-M`) | result | rule |
|---|---|---|
| `TypeName(apple)` | `Integer` | first letter in range |
| `TypeName(mango)` | `Integer` | range is **inclusive at both ends** |
| `TypeName(zebra)` | `Empty` | outside the range: an ordinary Variant |
| `Dim explicitVar As String` | `String` | an explicit `Dim` **overrides** the directive |
| `kilos$ = "text"` | `String` | a **type suffix overrides** it too |
| `quantity = 2.6` | **3**, `Integer` | coerces on store, exactly like `Dim x As Integer` |
| `amount = 2.5` | **2** | half-to-even, as everywhere else in VB6 |

### Overlapping ranges are a compile error

`DefInt A-M` followed by `DefStr A-C` does **not** resolve by last-wins or first-wins. `vb6.exe` refuses
the module:

```
Compile Error in File 'Module1.bas', Line 1 : Duplicate Deftype statement
```

Discovered by a probe that was trying to measure precedence and could not compile — which is the answer.
Any letter covered by two directives is rejected before the program runs, so an interpreter never has to
decide which wins.

### Why this is a lookup and not a map

The whole implementation is a letter-range → type table consulted when an undeclared variable is created.
No relationship between symbols appears anywhere in it, which is why it sits inside the pre-pass boundary
in `CLAUDE.md` rather than against it.

### Everything a DefType types, measured (2026-10-23, #169)

Measured on vb6.exe, native and p-code identical, under en-GB. Each program `DefTypeTests` pins was made as written.

**Overturned, and it was ours.** The section above says DefType "cannot be measured with `Option Explicit` on at all",
being a rule about undeclared variables. It is wider than that: it types every declaration with no As clause, and those
exist under `Option Explicit`. With `Option Explicit` and `DefInt A-Z`, `Dim x` then `x = 2.6` is an Integer 3, and
`Function F()` returns an Integer.

Under `DefBool B`, `DefByte Y`, `DefInt I-J, K`, `DefLng N`, `DefCur C`, `DefSng S`, `DefDbl D`, `DefDate T`, `DefStr Z`,
`DefObj O` and `DefVar V`:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `b1 = 1` | Boolean True |
| `y1 = 300`, then `y1 = 200` | 6, then Byte 200 |
| `i1 = 2.6`, `j1 = 2.5` | Integer 3, Integer 2 |
| `k1 = 40000` | 6 |
| `n1 = 70000` | Long 70000 |
| `c1 = 1.23456` | Currency 1.2346 |
| `s1 = 1.5`, `d1 = 1.5` | Single, Double |
| `t1 = 2` | Date, serial 2 |
| `z1 = 5` | String "5" |
| `Set o1 = New Collection` | Collection |
| `v1 = 5` | a Variant holding an Integer |
| `a1 = 2.6`, no DefType covering A | Double |
| `i9`, `z9`, `o9`, `b9`, `t9`, `v9`, never assigned | Integer 0, String "", Nothing, Boolean, Date, Empty |
| `Dim i5, z5, a5, i6(2)` | Integer, String, Empty, `Integer()` |
| module-level `Dim im, zm, am` | Integer, String, Empty |
| `Const I8 = 2.6`, `Const Z8 = 5` | **Double 2.6, Integer**: a Const keeps its value's type |
| `Function IFun()` returning 2.6 | Integer 3 |
| `Function ZFun()` returning 5 | String |
| `Sub ITake(i7)` given 2.6 | Integer 3 inside it |
| `Sub ZTake(ByVal z7)` given 5 | String "5" inside it |
| `Static is1`, then `is1 = is1 + 1` twice | Integer 1, then 2 |
| `For i3 = 1 To 2` | Integer 3 after it |
| `Set a2 = New Collection`, `a2` never declared, no DefType covering A | Collection: a Set declares as a Let does |
| `i2 = 2.6` in another module with no DefType | Double: a DefType is its own module's |
| a class's own `DefInt A-Z`: field `cnt`, local `q`, `Function Count()` | Integer, Integer 3, Integer |
| `DefStr Z-X`, then `x = 5` | String: a range written backwards covers X to Z |
| `DefInt a-c`, then `b = 2.6` | Integer 3: lower case names the same letters |

**DefObj**, under `DefObj O`:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `Dim o5`, and module-level `Dim om` | Nothing, Nothing |
| `Set o5 = New Collection`, `Set om = New Collection` | Collection, Collection |
| `o5 = 5`, `o5` holding a Collection | 438 |
| `Dim o8`, then `o8 = 5` | 91 |
| `o6 = 5`, `o6` never declared | 91 |
| `Function OFun()` with `Set OFun = New Collection` | Collection |
| `Sub OTake(o7)` given a Collection, then Nothing | Collection, Nothing |
| `o7 = 5` in `Sub OLet(o7)` given Nothing | 91 |
| `OBad = 5` in `Function OBad()` before any Set | 91, and the call returns Nothing |

So DefObj makes each of these an `As Object`. A `Function F() As Object` and a `Function F() As Collection` that are
never Set behave the same way: `TypeName` is Nothing and `Is Nothing` is True. A Let into the first's name before a Set
is 91. A Let into the second's does not compile ("Argument not optional"), as for a variable.

**A DefType'd variable is a typed operand** (#122), as a Dim'd one is. Under `DefInt P`:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `p1 = 30000`, then `p1 * 3` | 6 |
| `p9 + 32767 + 1`, `p9` never assigned | 6 |
| `Dim p5`, then `p5 = 30000: p5 * 3` | 6 |
| `PFun() * 3`, `Function PFun()` returning 30000 | 6 |
| `b1 = 30000: b1 * 3`, no DefType covering B | Long 90000 |

**Where it must sit.** A DefType after any declaration is "Deftype statements must precede declarations". That holds
after a `Dim`, a `Public` or `Private` variable, a `Const` (Public or not), a `Type`, an `Enum` and a `Declare`. After
`Option Base`, `Option Compare` or another DefType it compiles. Inside a procedure it is "Invalid inside procedure".
After a procedure it is VB6's general "Only comments may appear after End Sub, End Function, or End Property", as
for a label there (see "Line labels", below). HexIDE gives that error for nothing at module level, so it runs such a module
with the DefType applied.

**The other compile errors:**
- `DefInt AB` is "Expected: letter".
- `DefDec E` is "Expected: line number or label or statement or end of statement". VB6 has no DefDec, though the
  grammar lexes it.
- `DefInt A-C` then `DefInt B` is "Duplicate Deftype statement", even though both are Integer. So is `DefInt A-Z` then
  `DefStr A-Z`.

**Two things HexIDE does not do yet**, measured here and filed:
- **A ReDim that declares.** Under `DefInt I`, `ReDim i4(2)` on a name never declared is `Integer()`, and `ReDim a4(2)`
  is `Variant()`. HexIDE refuses both as "Unknown variable" (#1495).
- **An undeclared variable passed ByRef.** With `Sub Bump(x As Integer)` and `i12` never declared, `Bump i12` twice
  leaves `i12` an Integer 2. Without DefType, `Bump a12` with `Sub Bump(x)` leaves an Integer 2, and `Fill b12` with
  `s = "filled"` leaves a String. HexIDE loses the write in all three (#1505). **Since fixed by #1505**; see "An
  undeclared variable passed ByRef".

### In HexIDE (#169)

`PrePass.VisitDeftypeStmt` collects each module's DefType statements into a 26-letter table, raising the compile errors
above, and `PrePass.DefaultTypeOf(name)` reads it. It is consulted wherever a declaration has no As clause:
- `StatementExecutor.AllocImplicitVariant`, for a variable made on first use, whether by a Let, a Set, a For or a
  statement that stores;
- `ExpressionExecutor`'s read of a name never assigned;
- `StatementExecutor.DeclareLocal`, for a `Dim`, a `Static`, a module's variable and a class's field;
- `PrePass.ParseParams` and `PrePass.ReturnOf`, for parameters and returns.

The slot the pre-pass hoists for a module-level variable is not typed. The module's Dim statement, run when the module
starts, makes the slot the program uses, and `DeclareLocal` types that one.

A type character on such a variable is #742 and #739.

## Variant arithmetic promotes; a declared type is a ceiling (2026-09-02, #122)

Re-measured because the rule as originally filed was wrong in a way that would have shipped a silent bug.

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `TypeName(30000)` | `Integer` — a literal is Integer |
| `a = 30000` (undeclared) | Variant, subtype `Integer` |
| `a = 30000 : b = 3 : a * b` | **`Long` / 90000** |
| `a = 30000 : b = 30000 : a + b` | **`Long` / 60000** |
| `a = 2000000000 : b = 3 : a * b` | **`Double` / 6000000000** |
| `a = 30000 : a * 3` (Variant × literal) | **`Long` / 90000** |
| `Dim a As Integer` × Variant `b` | **`Long` / 90000** — either side lifts it |
| Variant `b` × `Dim a As Integer` | **`Long` / 90000** — order irrelevant |
| **`30000 * 3` (literal × literal)** | **Err 6** |
| `Dim a As Integer` + literal `30000` | **Err 6** |
| `Dim a As Integer, b As Integer` … `a * b` | **Err 6** |
| `(a + 0) * 3`, `a` declared Integer | **Err 6** — fixedness **propagates** |
| untyped `Fact(10)` / `Fact(13)` | `3628800` **Long** / **Double** |

### The rule

> **If either operand is a Variant, the ceiling lifts and the result widens Integer → Long → Double by
> magnitude. If both operands are typed — declared *or literal* — the type is a ceiling and overflow is
> Err 6.**

Driven by **operand provenance**, not by the result. #122 originally recorded it as *"driven by the result,
not the operands"* with `30000 * 3` → 90000 at the head of its table; that row is wrong, and building to it
would have promoted `Dim i As Integer : i = i + 1` past 32767 in silence — the common shape, not a rare one.

Two consequences for any implementation:

- **A literal is fixed, not a Variant.** `Dim a As Integer` plus the literal 30000 raises Err 6.
- **Fixedness propagates through sub-expressions**, so it must ride on the *value*: `(a + 0)` keeps its
  ceiling. It cannot be looked up at the operator, because an operand may be a call result with no slot to
  interrogate — which is exactly the shape of `Fact = n * Fact(n - 1)`, the case #122 was filed from.

### And a correction to a wrong expectation of my own

`CStr(6000000000#)` is **`6000000000`**, not `6E+09`. VB6 does not switch a Double of that magnitude to
scientific notation. Recorded because a test was briefly written against the invented form.
## Member chains, including module-qualified ones (2026-09-02, #173)

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `p.In1.Z` (nested UDT field, unqualified) | `99` |
| `Module1.n` (module-qualified scalar) | `5` |
| `Module1.p.X` (qualified, then a field) | `7` |
| `Module1.p.In1.Z` (qualified, then **two** fields — four levels) | `42` |

No depth limit and no special case: a module qualifier is simply the first step of an ordinary chain, and
everything after it resolves exactly as it would unqualified. `Module1.p.In1.Z` is `Module1` → `p` → `In1`
→ `Z`, evaluated left to right.

Worth stating because HexIDE refused the qualified form with *"Multi-level qualified member access is not
supported"* while already folding the unqualified `p.In1.Z` correctly — the two were treated as different
problems when only the first step differs in kind (a namespace rather than a value).

## Implements, and interface-typed variables (2026-09-02, #186)

Measured with `scripts/vb6-oracle.ps1 -Classes`, added for this: the harness could only ever compile one
`.bas`, so **the entire object model was unmeasurable**. Implements, `As New`, `Set` type-enforcement,
default members and parameterized properties all need at least one class module and several need two.

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `Dim x As IFoo : Set x = New Bar : x.Area()` | **7** — dispatched to `IFoo_Area` |
| `TypeName(x)` where `x As IFoo` holds a `Bar` | **`Bar`** — the concrete class, not the interface |
| `TypeName(New Bar)` | `Bar` |
| `TypeOf b Is IFoo`, `b` implements it | **True** |
| `TypeOf b Is IFoo`, `b` does **not** | **False** — not an error |
| `IFoo_Draw` declared **Public** rather than Private | **accepted** — the Private convention is not enforced |
| `x.Own` where `x As IFoo` and `Own` is `Bar`'s own member | **compile error**, *"Method or data member not found"* |
| a class declaring `Implements IFoo` but omitting a member | **compile error**, see below |

### The two compile errors, verbatim

An interface-typed variable exposes **only the interface's members**. Reaching for the concrete class's own
member fails, in the module that does it:

```
Compile Error in File 'Module1.bas', Line 19 : Method or data member not found
```

And a class that claims an interface must supply all of it — reported against the *class*, naming both the
missing member and the interface:

```
Compile Error in File 'Partial.cls', Line 0 : Object module needs to implement 'Erase2' for interface 'IFoo'
```

That second message is the one HexIDE should reproduce. Per the approximation rule in `CLAUDE.md` and
`interpreter-core:40-42`, it is raised **when the class is first instantiated** rather than before the
program runs — the conformance data (both member tables) is already collected by `PrePass`, so the check
itself needs no binding. A class never instantiated is never checked, which is the accepted
error-on-a-path-never-taken divergence.

### What a class-typed slot refuses

A slot declared `As <class>` enforces that name on every `Set`. Measured with `On Error GoTo` (see the
harness note below), the error is the same in both directions and carries no interface-specific message:

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `Dim c As Bar : Set c = New Baz` (unrelated classes) | **Err 13**, `Type mismatch` |
| `Dim x As IFoo : Set x = New Baz` (`Baz` does not implement `IFoo`) | **Err 13**, `Type mismatch` |
| `Set v = New Bar` (`v As Variant`), then `Set x = v` (`x As IFoo`) | **accepted** |

The third row is the interesting one: routing a reference through a Variant does not launder it, and does not
break it either. The check reads the OBJECT, not the declared type of wherever the reference came from — a
Variant has no declared type to check against, and the `Set` into `x` still succeeds because `Bar` really does
implement `IFoo`.

### Harness note: `On Error Resume Next` does not trap inside a `-Declarations` function

Found while measuring the above, and it silently corrupts results, so it is worth stating plainly. A probe
function of the form

```vb
Function P()
    On Error Resume Next
    ' ...something that errors...
    P = "n=" & CStr(Err.Number)
End Function
```

returns **nothing**, and the error surfaces on the harness's own outer trap instead. A control probe that
merely does `Err.Raise 5` behaves the same way, so this is not specific to the error being measured. The same
function written with `On Error GoTo H` works correctly and returns the number and description.

**Use `On Error GoTo` in `-Declarations` probe functions.** `On Error Resume Next` remains fine in the
expression-level harness, which is where the rest of this document's error numbers came from. The cause has
not been established, so this is recorded as a measured harness behaviour rather than explained.

## Static locals (2026-09-02)

Measured before implementing anything, because the design branches on the answer and two plausible
positions were both on the table. Nothing here is implemented yet — `Static x As Long` throws, and
`Static Sub` is silently accepted with the modifier discarded, which is worse (see `interpreter-gaps.md`).

| probe | measured |
|---|---|
| `Static n As Long` inside a class module method | **compiles** — legal, not a VB6 error |
| two instances of that class, `a` bumped 3x and `b` once | **3/1** — storage is PER-INSTANCE |
| `Static Function` with an ordinary `Dim k` inside, called 3x | **3** — the modifier makes ALL locals static |
| plain `Function`, `Static n` + `Dim m`, called 3x, reported as `n * 10 + m` | **31** — n persists, m resets |

### What this overturned

The expectation going in was that VB6 might not permit `Static` in a class module at all — a reasonable
guess, since per-instance static storage is an odd thing for a language to offer and there is no analogue
in most of the family. It permits it, and it does the more expensive thing: each instance gets its own
copy. Had we implemented on the guess, a class with a `Static` counter would have shared one counter
across every instance, which is a silent wrong answer rather than a crash.

The `Static Function` row matters for a different reason: the modifier is not a shorthand, it genuinely
changes the storage class of every local in the procedure. HexIDE currently parses it and throws the
modifier away, so such a procedure runs with ordinary locals and quietly produces wrong numbers.

### What it means for the implementation

Static storage cannot hang off `ProcedureInfo`, because that is shared by every instance. For a class
module method it belongs on the `VbObject`, keyed by procedure and name, and it dies with the instance.
For a standard module the two are indistinguishable (the module is a singleton), so a per-procedure table
is correct there.

The slot model already does the hard part: `ExecutionState` holds slots by id and `ExecutionEnvironment`
binds names to them, so a static local is "look up or create the slot, bind the name to it, and do NOT add
it to `ownedSlots`" — the last part being what keeps scope-exit from releasing it and firing a premature
`Class_Terminate`. Recursion then shares the slot without any extra work, which is what VB6 does.

## Omitted optional arguments, and string operands to numeric intrinsics (2026-09-02)

Measured to check two defects an adversarial pass reported against HexIDE. Both were real; one was
described wrongly, in a way that would have produced the wrong fix.

| probe | VB6 | HexIDE |
|---|---|---|
| `Split("a b c", , 2)` | **`n=1 [a][b c]`** — 2 elements on the default space delimiter | returns the whole string as ONE element |
| `Split("a,b,c", ",", , 1)` | **`n=2 [a]`** — 3 elements, compare arg accepted | raises **Err 13** |
| `Abs("abc")` | **Err 13** | Err 13 — correct |
| `Abs("5")` | **`5`** | Err 13 — wrong |

### The omitted-argument hole

A skipped middle argument (`Split(s, , 2)`) must take the parameter's default. HexIDE materialises a blank
call-site slot as `Vb6Value.Missing`, but `VB6BuiltIns.Array.HasArg` tests `!= EmptyVariant`, so the guard
never fires: the delimiter becomes `AsStr(Missing)` = `""`, and the empty-delimiter branch returns the
input unsplit. Skipping `limit` is worse than a wrong answer — `a.Count >= 3` is satisfied by the blank
slot, `AsInt(Missing)` falls past every case, and it throws. `Filter` shares the bug.

The comment above `HasArg` asserts that a skipped optional "arrives as Empty". That is wrong about this
interpreter's own call machinery, and the wrong comment is what kept the bug alive.

### Why the `Abs` row needed the oracle

The report was "a String operand raises Err 13", offered as the defect. **VB6 raises Err 13 there too**,
so taken at face value it would have led to making `Abs("abc")` return something — a change away from
VB6, not toward it.

The real divergence is narrower and opposite in shape: VB6 accepts a *numeric* string and rejects a
non-numeric one; HexIDE rejects **both**, because `TryNumericToDouble` switches only over the numeric CLR
types plus `DateTime` and returns false for `String`. The same path is shared by `Sqr`, `Sgn`, `Sin`,
`Cos`, `Exp`, `Log`, `Tan`, `Atn`, `Hex`, `Oct`, `CDate` and `CBool`, so one fix covers all of them —
which is only visible once the boundary is stated correctly.

This is the second time a plausible-sounding defect report would have moved HexIDE *away* from VB6 if
implemented as written. Measure the claim, not just the behaviour it complains about.

### Return widths of the integer-returning intrinsics (2026-09-02)

Found while fixing #190, when a test asserted the wrong type and the oracle disagreed with both of us.
Then measured across the whole family before fixing (#193), which turned up two the original finding had
missed.

| `TypeName` in VB6 | intrinsics |
|---|---|
| **Long** | `Len`, `InStr`, `InStrRev`, `LBound`, `UBound`, `DateDiff`, **`VarType`** |
